claims.text: High-throughput screening can rapidly narrow the vast HEA compositional space.
A machine-learning-based screening framework can predict intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA compositions.
The machine-learning framework will outperform conventional thermo-kinetic design methods.
The refractory HEA compositional space is broad and largely unexplored.
Most refractory HEA candidates have been evaluated using time-intensive experiments and simulations.
Machine-learning models should be trained on existing experimental data and simulation outputs using compositional descriptors.
Mixing enthalpy, atomic size mismatch, and density govern microstructural evolution and phase stability.
Microstructural evolution and phase stability mediate alloy strength, ductility, and weight.
A machine-learning model can learn correlations between compositional descriptors and strength, ductility, and density from prior datasets.
Learned descriptor-property correlations enable rapid identification of alloys having balanced microstructures.
High-throughput computational screening can discover lightweight HEAs with enhanced room- and elevated-temperature strength.
The proposed framework will produce statistically significant simultaneous improvements in intrinsic strength, ductility, and density relative to conventionally designed alloys.
Conventional iterative thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation are too time-consuming to navigate the compositional landscape efficiently.
The machine-learning approach is limited to composition ranges represented in its training data.
Predictive accuracy may decline for extreme descriptor values or previously unseen elemental combinations.
Omission of relevant processing or microstructural factors from the training data may reduce predictive accuracy and generalizability.
